expected_text_segments:
Update: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission plans November 9 data roundtable

The SEC wants feedback on machine-understandable data and Super Intelligence. November 9 is a discussion to follow, not a rule change to assume.

What to watch: Listen for concrete examples of use, a clear account of risks and costs, and any stated next steps. These are watchpoints for the discussion, not promised agenda items or conclusions.

Read the full brief: https://capitalchronicle.substack.com/p/us-securities-and-exchange-commission

Analysis, not financial advice. Readers decide whether to trade.

media_manifest.alt_text: SEC roundtable facts: November 9, 2026, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. EST, at SEC headquarters in Washington, D.C., with public access and a live stream on SEC.gov. The announced topic is machine-understandable data, Super Intelligence, and related risks and costs.
media_manifest.caption: The SEC's October 19 announcement schedules a public roundtable for November 9. The stated discussion concerns machine-understandable data, Super Intelligence and associated risks and costs.
